checklist_item.title: Verify Conditional Scope: Pre-EIP-155 cross-chain replay vulnerability awareness
checklist_item.test_procedure: 1. Verify that v == 27 or v == 28 indicates pre-EIP-155 transaction. 2. Check if client defaults to pre-155 signing under any circumstances. 3. Verify warnings are displayed when handling pre-155 transactions. 4. Document any Fusaka-specific changes to pre-155 behavior. 5. Check that pre-155 transactions are still valid but flagged appropriately.
checklist_item.notes: Source: PROP-0005. CONDITIONAL SCOPE - Known design limitation. Only in-scope if Fusaka changes alter pre-155 behavior.

phase1_abstract_interpretation.summary: This checklist item targets EIP-155 replay protection logic in a Python EVM implementation (v == 27 or v == 28 check for pre-EIP-155 transactions). Prysm is a Go Ethereum consensus client (beacon chain) and does not implement transaction signing, EIP-155 validation, or any EVM execution layer transaction processing. An exhaustive search of the target_workspace Go codebase for 'begin_transaction', 'copy_trie', '_snapshots', 'transient_storage', 'created_accounts' returns zero results. The only EIP155 references found are: a genesis config parameter (EIP155Block) and an end-to-end test helper calling go-ethereum's EIP155Signer to drive a separate execution client — neither represents Prysm implementing EIP-155 logic. There is no state to analyze for this property in Prysm.
phase1_abstract_interpretation.cache_analysis: Not applicable. Prysm does not implement transaction signing or EIP-155 v-value checks. No state related to this property exists in the codebase.
phase1_abstract_interpretation.concurrency_analysis: Not applicable. No concurrent access to EIP-155 transaction signing state exists in Prysm.

phase2_symbolic_execution.summary: No code paths exist in Prysm to execute symbolically for this property. The v == 27/v == 28 pre-EIP-155 check, default signing behavior, and pre-155 transaction flagging all reside in the execution layer (e.g., go-ethereum or Python ethereum-specs), not in the consensus client. Constructing an exploit path is impossible because there is no entry point into transaction signing logic in Prysm. The Fusaka-specific changes audited in this branch (beacon chain / consensus layer) do not modify EIP-155 behavior.
phase2_symbolic_execution.timing_dependencies: None — no code exists to trigger.

phase2_5_reachability_analysis.summary: There is no reachable code in Prysm corresponding to EIP-155 transaction signing or pre-EIP-155 replay protection. Prysm's attack surface is beacon chain P2P (libp2p gossip, Req/Resp protocols), validator RPC (gRPC/REST), and execution engine API (Engine API JSON-RPC to the execution client). None of these interfaces expose EIP-155 transaction signing logic in Prysm itself.
phase2_5_reachability_analysis.attack_surface: This property is entirely in the execution layer. Prysm has no attack surface for EIP-155 replay attacks.

phase3_invariant_proving.summary: The invariant 'v == 27 or v == 28 must be detected and handled as pre-EIP-155' cannot be evaluated against Prysm because Prysm does not process transaction v-values. The Fusaka changes in the audited branch do not introduce any transaction signing code. The invariant is vacuously satisfied (no violating code exists) but for the wrong reason — the functionality is simply absent.
phase3_invariant_proving.guard_sufficiency: Not applicable — no guard to evaluate. The property belongs to the execution client layer.

phase3_5_scope_filtering.reason: The CONDITIONAL SCOPE note on this item explicitly states it is only in-scope if Fusaka changes alter pre-155 behavior. The Fusaka changes in OffchainLabs/prysm are consensus layer changes. Prysm does not implement EIP-155 transaction signing at all. The genesis config reference to EIP155Block is a chain configuration parameter passed to the execution client — it does not constitute Prysm implementing EIP-155 logic. No Fusaka change in this branch touches transaction replay protection.
phase3_5_scope_filtering.recommendation: Close as out-of-scope for Prysm. If EIP-155 behavior in the context of Fusaka is a concern, the audit should target the execution client (e.g., go-ethereum / geth with Fusaka support) rather than the consensus client.

checklist_item.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Does snapshot mechanism provide true deep-copy isolation?
checklist_item.test_procedure: 1. Review copy_trie implementation for deep vs shallow copy. 2. Create nested snapshots via contract calls. 3. Mutate state in inner call and verify outer snapshot remains unaffected. 4. Test rollback_transaction restores exact state from begin_transaction. 5. Check both _main_trie and _storage_tries are properly copied.
checklist_item.notes: Source: PROP-0006. Boundary: tb-003. Shallow copy would break transaction atomicity.

checklist_item.title: Is the snapshot count invariant maintained after begin_transaction?
